findings.claim: The reworked q18 context adds 'decide what the compiler infers' when legacy raw-type code hands data to a generic method. If the raw-typed expression itself is the argument, the method is applicable only by unchecked conversion, and JLS 15.12.2.6 then makes the invocation's type the erasure of the declared return type (for example Object instead of T), so assigning the result to a String does not compile. That rule is counter-intuitive and is not taught: the generics page teaches inference only from the argument or the assignment target with type-safe arguments. The section 8 raw-type rule (line 204) does not cover inference. Sources (not fetched in this review; cited for verification): https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.12.2.6; https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-5.html#jls-5.1.9; collections-streams/collections-in-depth/generics/artifact.html ('a type variable is inferred from the argument or, if absent there, from the assignment target').
findings.recommendation: Add to the raw-type rule: in q18 the generic method receives a parameterized reference (for example a List<String> polluted earlier through a raw alias), so the inferred type argument is the taught 'from the argument' case; never pass a raw-typed expression to the generic method or key an outcome that depends on JLS 15.12.2.6 return-type erasure.

findings.claim: The reworked q19 context uses put, get and getOrDefault on a map with wrapper values, and the q19 rule lets it locate 'unboxing null'. Map.getOrDefault returns the default only when the key has no mapping; for a key mapped to null it returns null, which then fails on unboxing. That is untaught (the wrapper page shows getOrDefault only as the 'safe map read'), so combining a null-valued key with getOrDefault would key untaught behavior. The rule's list of taught boxing sites also omits getOrDefault's default argument, which is boxed like a put argument. Sources (not fetched in this review; cited for verification): https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Map.html#getOrDefault(java.lang.Object,V); collections-streams/collections-in-depth/wrapper-types-and-autoboxing/artifact.html ('Safe map read int n = counts.getOrDefault("x", 0);').
findings.recommendation: Extend the q19 rule: unboxing null comes only from get on an absent key; no key is mapped to a null value; getOrDefault's default argument counts as a boxing site like a put argument.

findings.claim: Reworked q17 ('choose the code that does it safely') keys 'the safe removal method' (line 202), but lists#o2 and the lists page teach two equally safe methods, Iterator.remove and removeIf, and section 6 (line 173) records that q17 has a stream-based distractor; reassigning the variable to a filtered stream result also removes the records unless the stem requires the same list object to change. Without a rule, q17 can have two defensible answers. Sources (not fetched in this review; cited for verification): collections-streams/collections-in-depth/lists-sets-and-maps-in-depth/artifact.html ('remove with the iterator's own remove() or with removeIf'); https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/stream/Stream.html#toList().
findings.recommendation: Add a q17 rule: at most one of Iterator.remove and removeIf is a defensible option, and the stem requires the existing shared list to change in place, so any stream-based option is unambiguously wrong.

findings.claim: The new q30 context (choose the stream pipeline equivalent to a loop that filters, transforms and sorts loaded records) has no section 8 rule defining 'equivalent'. A loop builds a modifiable ArrayList while Stream.toList() (the only collector the plan allows) returns an unmodifiable list, so if the loop's result is later modified the pipeline is not equivalent; sorting before versus after map changes the element type the comparator sees. Stability is not a trap (List.sort and sorted() on an ordered stream are both stable), but the item needs that stated so the key holds. Sources (not fetched in this review; cited for verification): https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/stream/Stream.html#toList(); https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/stream/Stream.html#sorted(java.util.Comparator); https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/List.html#sort(java.util.Comparator).
findings.recommendation: Add a q30 rule: equivalence means the same elements in the same order; the loop's result is not modified afterwards (or the stem says the result is read-only); distractors differ by a visible filter, map or sort-key change, never by mutability or sort stability alone.
